title: The co-founders story: setting up a digital humanitarian network
html:
Have you ever wondered how to setup up a network similar to the Digital Humanitarian Network (DHNetwork) within a country or a specific crisis? Essentially, a network-of-networks that aims to bring digitally-enabled groups together to support each other and formal organizations when responding to humanitarian crisis? Ever since launching the DHNetwork in early 2012, Patrick Meier and I have been regularly approached about setting up similar networks at a more local or regional level. Our answers were often ad hoc, pointing to the best resources and contacts we could think of at the moment. There was no guidance on how to create a DHNetwork.

At the 2014 DHNetwork Summit, the topic of local DHNetworks was explored further. General consensus was that local DHNetworks would be able to respond quicker, be more inline with the needs, be able to connect with local responders and be able to increase resilience. A local DHNetwork would bring together local Volunteer & Technical Communities, including local chapters of global groups, with local formal organizations to make sure everyone was connected in-country pre-crisis. They would learn about each other, figure out how to work together, and be ready to respond together in the future. If needed during a crisis, they could reach out to the DHNetwork Global, or other nearby DHNetwork Local instances, for extra support.

But without even basic guidance, how could we expect local DHNetwork entities to be created? We needed to pull together the knowledge of digital community builders with our DHNetwork history and put a concrete document together. We needed to fill that guidance gap.

This fall I have paired up with Jennie Phillips, who is studying how to develop resilience in digital response networks, to draft guidance on how to create a local DHNetwork. We are aiming to have a solid draft ready by mid-December and a polished version ready in early 2016.

To start, we wanted to tell the the co-founders’ stories leading up to the DHNetwork creation. Patrick and I wrote down the key events that either of us were directly involved with and we felt helped lead to the DHNetwork creation. From that, Jennie and Ignacio Gimenez-Rebollo set out to tell the story in a one-page graphic (see below), which will be included in the guidance document. I particularly like that, although we often think of time as linear, the curved line shows that the process was anything but linear or intended.

[PDF 500 KB]

Of course what you do not see in this graphic is all the various member organizations, and their countless hard working volunteers, who both “make the magic happen” and constructively engage in the continual evolution of the the DHNetwork. Without them, there would be no network.

More on this topic in early 2016.

Andrej
